Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1) Manage suspected acute asthma exacerbation at home with stepped-up controller and reliever therapy; arrange timely in-person assessment.
- 2) Schedule GP (or nurse) asthma review within the next few days; perform chest exam and peak flow during assessment; consider antibiotics/steroids only if indicated by exam findings.
- 3) Optimize and monitor asthma maintenance therapy in interim: increase inhaled corticosteroid dose (brown inhaler) and adjust short-acting beta-agonist use; provide clear red-flag instructions to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen.
- 4) Document and review atopy history (hay fever and eczema); continue current topical therapies as discussed; no new agents initiated today.
- 5) Reinforce home peak flow monitoring and ensure follow-up of results at the next visit.

Subjective:

- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began about 2–3 days ago and have persisted.
- History of present illness: Uses blue inhaler (Salbutamol) with symptoms; reports using it daily and as a preventive, including morning and evening use.
- Medications:
  - Salbutamol inhaler (blue) – use as-needed; dose/frequency not documented.
  - Beclomethasone inhaler (Clenil, brown) – current use; dose/frequency not documented.
  - Hydrocortisone (topical) and Cetraben (emollient) – for eczema; dose/frequency not documented.
  - History noted: eczema and hay fever; family history of asthma (brother); last asthma attack 3–4 years ago; last asthma review with nurse ~2 years ago.
- Allergies: Environmental allergies (hay fever); no drug allergies reported.
- Social history: Not documented.
- Review of systems: No sputum produced; no fever reported beyond hay fever history.

Objective:
- Symptoms/Examination:
  - Shortness of breath with wheeze; coughing reported.
  - No sputum production.
  - Peak flow measurement at baseline discussed: approximately 380 (patient reports this is their normal peak flow).
- Procedures/tests performed today: Chest examination not yet performed in this visit; peak flow measurement to be performed during assessment (planned).
- Medications currently used (as per patient report): Salbutamol inhaler; Clenil inhaler; Hydrocortisone; Cetraben.
- Allergies: Hay fever noted as environmental allergy; no medication allergies.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Issue: Acute asthma exacerbation (current symptoms with SOB, wheeze, and requiring frequent use of reliever inhaler)
   - Assessment: Acute asthma exacerbation (history suggests poor control over past 2–3 days; prior control was good).
   - Differential diagnosis: Not documented.
   - Investigations planned: Chest examination and peak flow assessment at next contact; consideration of peak flow monitoring.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Increase Clenil (brown inhaler) to 4 puffs twice daily.
     - Salbutamol (blue inhaler) for relief up to every 2 hours as needed (avoid excessive use; frequent use indicates worsening control).
     - If symptoms worsen or frequent relief use continues, patient should attend A&E.
     - Potential antibiotics and/or systemic steroids may be considered depending on chest exam and peak flow results.
   - Referrals: Schedule an in-person GP assessment within the next few days for formal asthma review.

2. Issue: Asthma control and monitoring needs
   - Assessment: Asthma previously well controlled; current symptom cluster suggests an asthma exacerbation and need for review.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not documented.
   - Investigations planned: Review home peak flow monitoring; perform in-clinic peak flow assessment during the upcoming visit.
   - Treatment planned: Continue gradual uptitration of controller therapy (Clenil) as above; reinforce SABA use guidelines; emphasize follow-up with primary care.
   - Referrals: In-person asthma review with GP within the next few days.

3. Issue: Atopy history (hay fever and eczema)
   - Assessment: History of hay fever and eczema; no documented drug allergies.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.
   - Investigations planned: None at this time.
   - Treatments planned: Continue current topical therapies (Cetraben emollient and hydrocortisone) as previously used; no changes at this visit.
   - Referrals: None indicated for atopy at this time.
